> The OMNI stand is a compact, 3D-printable desktop organizer designed to eliminate cable clutter and streamline nightstand or workspace layout. It features a top-loading circular recess custom-fitted for my watch, allowing effortless charger removal on the go. Directly behind the watch module is an integrated ergonomic vertical arm to hold my headphones.

## Design

### 2026-10-16 – # October 12: Base Block & Initial Layout

**5.5h**

# October 12: Base Block & Initial Layout

Started the OMNI Stand project in Onshape with the goal of designing a compact 120x120mm desktop charging station to organize my Galaxy Watch 8 and Sony WH-CH-720N headphones.

For this session, I created a center rectangle on the top plane, dimensioned it to 120mm x 120mm, and extruded it upward by 30mm to form the main solid base block. To give it a sleek, modern, and print-safe finish, I applied a 12mm fillet to all four vertical outer corners.

![Screenshot 2026-10-14 233027](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/MqfXtqzyoV3kC5NbjDzdPoc1zza7pyWb/82b6fccf5e8ceb9c3f9b4145a3be3929c53b1cb37d677820d938c886d8db9cd8.png)
**Total time spent: 1.5 hours**

---

# October 13: Watch Puck Recess & Rear Cable Slot

Next, I focused on integrating the smartwatch charging module. I created a new sketch on the top surface of the base and drew a 32mm circular profile custom-sized to fit the magnetic charging puck for the Galaxy Watch 8 (44mm).

Using the Extrude-Remove feature, I cut a 7mm deep pocket so the puck sits flush. I also added a rear drop-in cable slot (4mm wide) running from the back of the puck recess to the rear edge of the base, allowing the charging cord to be inserted or removed easily without fishing it through a closed tunnel.

![Screenshot 2026-10-14 233141](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/MqfXtqzyoV3kC5NbjDzdPoc1zza7pyWb/f0cb8360bdc3394953b9f2922b3c3c0c6a94ed616fbd38fa4d6324f80c7e8b33.png)

**Total time spent: 2 hours**

---

# October 14: Vertical Headphone Arm & Height Optimization

For the headphone stand component, I sketched a rectangular profile (25mm x 40mm) on the top surface behind the watch puck recess.

I initially tested an extrusion height of 180mm–190mm, but after checking the physical dimensions and minimum clearance required for the Sony WH-CH-720N over-ear headphones, I increased the vertical arm length to **245 mm** to ensure the earcups hang freely without hitting the desk. Finally, I applied fillets to the top edges of the arm to create a smooth, curved headband rest that prevents creasing or damage to the cushion.

![Screenshot 2026-10-14 234000](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/MqfXtqzyoV3kC5NbjDzdPoc1zza7pyWb/56cff4c993853a7ede6d4a02a538a89b1e9167129298b1953990479232625a44.png)

**Total time spent: 2 hours**
